events.title: The election of Pope St. Gregory VII
events.shortBlurb: The monk Hildebrand became pope and gave his name to a sweeping reform of the Church…
body: On 22 April 1073, the Roman clergy and people acclaimed the archdeacon Hildebrand as pope, and he took the name Gregory VII. For years he had been the driving force behind the reform of the Roman Church, and now he set himself to carry it through with unbending resolve.

The Gregorian Reform attacked the buying and selling of Church offices and the marriage of clergy, and above all fought lay investiture — the control of bishoprics by kings and nobles. This brought Gregory into a titanic struggle with the Emperor Henry IV, whom he excommunicated and who came as a penitent to Canossa in 1077.
Driven at last from Rome, Gregory died in exile at Salerno in 1085, but the movement that bears his name reshaped the medieval Church and vindicated its independence. He was later canonized.
